prompt.context: Rock Energy is an Oil & Gas company evaluating the purchase of one of three oil fields in Latin America. After selecting which oil field to purchase, Rock Energy will outsource all drilling-related activities.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate the three oil fields, and which oil field should Rock Energy purchase?

clarifying_info.q: What rights does the purchase include?
clarifying_info.a: The rights allow Rock Energy to drill during year 1 and produce oil for 20 years. No oil is produced until the beginning of year 2.

clarifying_info.q: How many rigs can operate in each region?
clarifying_info.a: A maximum of 10 rigs can be deployed concurrently in each region.

clarifying_info.q: What does the cost per rig day include?
clarifying_info.a: The cost per rig day includes crew, consumables, and services.
Any amount of oil extracted will be sold at the current spot market price.

clarifying_info.q: Are there maintenance costs during the production phase?
clarifying_info.a: For simplicity, assume oil wells produce the same amount of oil for all 20 years with no maintenance costs.

clarifying_info.q: What is the upfront cost to acquire rights in each region?
clarifying_info.a: The rights to extract oil cost $40M in each region.

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of oil?
clarifying_info.a: The price of oil is $50 per barrel (bbl).

exhibits.title: Oil Field Profiles, 2010
exhibits.shows: A table comparing three regions across five operational dimensions: drilling rate (meters/day), average well depth (meters), maximum concurrent rigs, average well production (barrels per day), and cost per rig day.

data.note: Wells are continuously dug during year 1 (assume 360 days). Oil is extracted beginning of year 2. Once a well is completed the rig moves on to dig another well.

framework: Revenue side: price of oil × barrels produced per well × number of wells drilled per year
Cost side: rights acquisition cost (fixed, $40M) + variable drilling cost (days to drill × cost per rig day × number of wells)
Profitability: total revenue minus total cost; compare across all three regions
Qualitative / risk factors: political stability, insurance, labor/unions, oil price volatility, oil quality differences, expected-value analysis on production uncertainty

questions.prompt: Calculate the time (in days) required to complete one well in each region.
questions.guidance: Time to complete a well = Average depth ÷ Drilling rate (penetration rate). Region 1: 1200÷20=60 days. Region 2: 2700÷30=90 days. Region 3: 3600÷20=180 days.

math.answer: Region 1 = 60 days, Region 2 = 90 days, Region 3 = 180 days per well

questions.prompt: Calculate the number of wells drilled per year in each region (10 rigs, 360-day year).
questions.guidance: Number of wells = (360 ÷ days per well) × number of rigs. Rigs cycle continuously so the multiplier is 360/time per well × 10.

math.setup: Number of wells = (360 ÷ days to complete one well) × 10 rigs
math.answer: Region 1 = 60 wells, Region 2 = 40 wells, Region 3 = 20 wells

questions.prompt: Calculate the cost per well and yearly revenue per well in each region, then determine profit per well and profit margin per well.
questions.guidance: Cost per well = days to complete × cost per rig day. Yearly revenue per well = price per bbl × daily production × 360 days. Profit per well = revenue − cost. Margin = profit ÷ cost.

math.setup: Cost per well = days × rig day cost; Yearly revenue per well = $50 × bbl/day × 360
math.answer: Profit per well: R1=$1.5M (500% margin), R2=$2.7M (300% margin), R3=$1.8M (50% margin)

questions.prompt: Calculate total field-level revenue, total cost (including $40M rights), and total profit for each region in the first year of production.
questions.guidance: Total revenue = yearly revenue per well × number of wells. Total cost = (cost per well × number of wells) + $40M rights. Profit = total revenue − total cost. Despite Region 1's superior per-well margin, Region 2 wins on absolute profit due to a favorable combination of well count and per-well economics. Region 3 is unprofitable.

math.setup: Total Revenue = (revenue per well) × wells; Total Cost = (cost per well × wells) + $40,000,000; Profit = Total Revenue − Total Cost
math.answer: Region 1 profit=$50M, Region 2 profit=$68M (highest), Region 3 profit=−$4M (loss)

brainstorming.prompt: What other factors or risks could affect the decision to invest in a particular region?

categories.name: Political & Regulatory
ideas: Political stability of the host country
Risk of expropriation or contract renegotiation

categories.name: Operational & Cost
ideas: Logistics and infrastructure availability in each region
Equipment availability and lead time for rigs

categories.name: Market & Revenue
ideas: Volatility of oil prices (spot market exposure)
Quality differences in crude oil across regions (affects realized price)
Currency risk if costs are local but revenue is in USD
Demand outlook and ability to sell all extracted volume

categories.name: Financial & Strategic
ideas: Expected-value analysis assigning probabilities to different production outcomes
Net Present Value (NPV) over the full 20-year production life
Capital allocation: could rights fees be lower in some regions through negotiation?
Optionality: ability to expand rigs beyond 10 if production is favorable

recommendation: Rock Energy should purchase the rights to Region 2, which generates the highest first-year profit of $68M

Although Region 1 has a superior per-well profit margin (500% vs 300%), Region 2's deeper wells and higher per-well production yield greater absolute profit once scaled across all wells drilled in year 1
Region 3 is unprofitable at current oil prices and should be rejected
risks: Oil price decline would disproportionately hurt Region 2 given its higher cost base per well
Political or regulatory instability in the Latin American region hosting Field 2 could impair operations
Actual production per well may fall short of the 200 bbl/day average (geological uncertainty)
Higher cost per rig day in Region 2 makes profitability more sensitive to drilling delays or overruns
next_steps: Conduct an NPV analysis over the full 20-year production horizon to confirm Region 2 remains optimal
Perform an expected-value analysis assigning probabilities to different production scenarios for each region
Assess political risk and insurance costs specific to each host country
Negotiate contract terms with drilling operator to cap cost per rig day risk
